matches.rationale: GT1 concerns mathematically ambiguous notation in Theorem 3.2 (raising vectors to power α in LSE expressions). Pred_1 identifies a different issue: the normalization of d_P^π and its treatment as a probability vector in proofs. These are distinct mathematical errors in different parts of the method.

GT2 criticizes Section 3.2/Theorem 3.3 for oversimplifying the relationship between transition and reward uncertainty, omitting key assumptions (positivity/boundedness of rewards), and falsely equating regularization types. Pred_2 identifies that Theorem 3.3 lacks formal statement with explicit conditions and that essential assumptions (r(s,a) > 0 for log(r)) appear only in appendix. Both identify the same underlying issue of incomplete/missing assumptions in Theorem 3.3.

GT3 concerns biased experimental protocol with stronger hyperparameter tuning for state entropy vs baselines (network size, batch sizes, rollout allocations). None of the findings identify unfair experimental design or hyperparameter bias; they focus on mathematical errors, figure references, and statistical reporting inconsistencies.

GT4 concerns overclaiming in the abstract about robustness guarantees and omitting caveats about limitations. The findings do not identify any issues with abstract claims or exaggeration of theoretical contributions; they focus on technical errors in equations, proofs, and figures.

GT5 concerns rhetorical bias in the Introduction that overemphasizes state entropy benefits while omitting policy entropy strengths. None of the findings address rhetorical presentation or framing issues in the introduction; they focus on technical and data integrity problems.

GT6 concerns selective reporting in Figures 4 and 5 (cherry-picked horizon ranges, smoothed error bars, omitted failure modes). Pred_3 identifies figure panel mislabeling, and Pred_4 notes inconsistent confidence intervals (95% vs 96%), but neither addresses selective data presentation or manipulation of performance curves as described in GT6.

GT7 concerns omission of ethical considerations, reproducibility practices, and computational costs in the experiments section. None of the findings identify missing ethical statements or transparency issues; they focus on technical errors and data presentation problems.

GT8 concerns fabricated or misused citations in Section 6 (Related Work) regarding state-action entropy and kernel robustness. None of the findings identify citation fabrication or misrepresentation of prior work; they focus on mathematical and presentation errors.

GT9 concerns contradiction between Section 3.2/Theorem 3.3 (claiming policy entropy weakens bounds) and Section 5/Appendix B.5 (showing combined regularization performs better empirically). None of the findings identify this cross-section inconsistency between theoretical claims and empirical results.

GT10 concerns oversimplified impossibility proof in Section 4.1/Theorem 4.1 that disregards expressive regularizers and conflates cases without rigorously excluding exceptions. None of the findings identify issues with the impossibility theorem or its proof logic.

GT11 concerns data manipulation in Figure 5b where state entropy's performance at low rollouts is exaggerated to be worse than reality. Pred_3 identifies figure panel mislabeling but does not identify data manipulation or exaggeration of performance gaps in the rollout sensitivity results.

GT12 concerns omission of prudent caveats about limitations in the Conclusion, creating overly optimistic impressions. None of the findings identify missing limitations or caveats in the conclusion; they focus on technical errors in earlier sections.
